queries: Epoch AI open-weight models lag behind closed frontier months

sources_considered.why: Independent measurement covering Jan to May 2026, published before the post.
Earlier window (2023 to Oct 2025); the newer analysis covers the target period.
About consumer-GPU models, a different scope.

receipt.public_excerpt: Since January 2026, the most capable open-weight models have lagged frontier closed models by an average of four months in the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), our aggregate measure of model capability.

evidence_items.explanation: An average four-month lag over Jan to May 2026 fits 'only a few months behind'.

receipt.public_excerpt: We find an average time gap of four months. This estimate would grow to six months if we required that the open-weight model’s point estimate for ECI be strictly higher

evidence_items.explanation: Even under the stricter test the lag is six months, still within a plain reading of 'a few months'.

unresolved_gaps: Epoch notes that open models may do worse on private benchmarks and that labs may hold back their best closed models, so the true gap could be larger.
